      <link>https://www.nrk.no/nyheter/voldshendelse-i-alta_-to-pagrepet-av-svensk-politi--1.18087404</link>
      <description>To personer ble natt til mandag pågrepet av svensk politi i forbindelse med voldshendelsen i Alta søndag morgen, skriver politiet i loggen.
De to personene er bosatt et annet sted i Norge, siktet for drapsforsøk mot en mann bosatt i Alta.
Politiet etterforsker nå bakgrunnen for at de to dro til Alta og oppsøkte den fornærmede.
Etterforskningen så langt har avdekket at det har vært en relasjon mellom partene fra tidligere av.

      <description>120 avviste asylsøkere i Danmark oppfyller kriteriene for å bli sendt til et retursenter i Rwanda neste år.
Det opplyser det danske utlendings- og integreringsdepartementet til DR.
Det er bare asylsøkere som ikke har barn eller er blitt dømt til kriminalitet som kan bli sendt til Rwanda, ifølge allmennkringkasteren. Dette skal gjelde 120 av 365 avviste asylsøkere.
Danmark er ett av fem EU-land som er enige om å etablere et felles retursenter for asylsøkere i Rwanda.</description>

      <link>https://www.nrk.no/sport/karoline-grotting-best-av-alle-pa-sesongapningens-siste-dag-_-skiskytter-imponerte-1.18086614</link>
      <description>Karoline Grøtting var best av samtlige kvinner under dagens 15 kilometer fristil på Beitostølen.
5 kilometer før mål sto kampen om seieren mellom Grøtting og Kristin Austgulen Fosnæs. Der var det altså Grøtting som til slutt trakk det lengste strået.
Grøtting stod over fredagens 10 kilometer på grunn av magesmerter i et forsøk på å spare seg til dagens distanse.
– Jeg er veldig glad for det nå, sier Grøtting til NRK etter målgang.
Skiskytter Ida Lien var dagens andre startende og gikk i mål til ledelse. Der ble hun værende til Grøtting overtok lederstolen.
Likevel holdt det til 3. plass for skiskytteren.
Heidi Weng vant fredagens 10 kilometer klassisk, men klarte ikke å gjenskape prestasjonen i dag. Allerede ved 6,2 kilometer hadde Weng 17 sekunder opp til teten.
Weng endte på 5. plass, 36 sekunder bak vinner.
Herrene skal ut på sin 15 kilometer klokken 13:00. Den kan du følge på NRK TV.</description>

      <description>Egil Selvik fortsetter å storspille i Brest-målet. Lørdag sikret han 1-0-seier borte mot Strasbourg ved å redde straffespark fem minutter på overtid.
Sraffen ble dømt etter en VAR-gjennomgang av en situasjon der ballen traff armen til Brest-spiller Mama Baldé, men det berget ikke hjemmelaget.
Brest tok ledelsen ved Noah Edjouma i det 22. minutt, etter en svak klarering av keeper Filip Jørgensen. Selvik forsvarte ledelsen med en rekke gode redninger og hjalp laget sitt til den tredje strake seieren i Ligue 1.
Selvik voktet Norges mål i nasjonsligaseieren over Wales for en uke siden, men han måtte overraskende sette seg på benken igjen da Norge knep gruppeseieren med 3-2-seier over Danmark i Parken tirsdag. Da var Ørjan Nyland tilbake i målet. Lørdag satt Nyland på benken for RB Leipzig.
Brest-seieren løftet laget til 6.-plass på tabellen. Strasbourg har bare tre lag bak seg på tabellen.

      <title>Medier: Anthropic-aksjen prises til 83 dollar</title>
      <link>https://www.nrk.no/nyheter/medier_-anthropic-aksjen-prises-til-83-dollar-1.18084614</link>
      <description>Aksjen til KI-giganten Anthropic får en pris på 83 dollar.
Det melder flere medier, blant annet The New York Times, Reuters og Wall Street Journal.
Det er ventet at aksjenoteringen til Anthropic blir en av verdens største noensinne.
Til sammen er det planlagt et salg av 825 millioner aksjer.</description>

Canadian icon Steven Page serves up a festive culinary favourite, crafting golden Holiday Latkes then lighting up the room with an iconic, signature performance of “Cheese Log” and “Brian Wilson”

Holiday Latkes with Smoked Salmon & Homemade Apple Sauce

Apple Sauce

  • 4 lbs apples (peeled, cored, and chopped)
  • ⅓ cup water
  • 2 tbsp fresh lemon juice
  • ½ to 1 tsp ground cinnamon
  • Sugar to taste (optional)
  1. Place the chopped apples, water, and lemon juice into a large saucepan or Dutch oven over medium heat.
  2. Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce the heat to low, cover, and let it simmer for 15 to 25 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the apples are very tender and falling apart.
  3. Remove the lid and stir in the cinnamon and sugar (if using).
  4. Remove from heat and use a potato masher for a chunky texture, or an immersion blender, food processor, or high-speed blender for a smooth puree.

Holiday Latkes

  • 1.5 to 2 lbs russet potatoes (peeled or unpeeled)
  • 1/2 medium yellow or white onion
  • 1 to 2 large eggs, lightly beaten
  • 2 to 4 tbsp matzo meal or all-purpose flour (plus an optional pinch of baking powder)
  • 1 tsp kosher salt and black pepper to taste
  • Neutral high-heat oil (such as canola, peanut, or vegetable oil) for frying
  1. Grate: Shred the potatoes and onion using the large holes of a box grater or a food processor grating disc.
  2. Drain moisture: Place the shreds in a clean kitchen towel or cheesecloth and squeeze out as much liquid as possible. (Tip: Let the drained liquid sit for a few minutes and scoop the settled white potato starch at the bottom back into your mixture for extra crispiness.)
  3. Mix batter: Stir the squeezed potatoes and onion together with the egg, matzo meal or flour, salt, and pepper until evenly combined.
  4. Heat oil: Pour about ¼ inch of oil into a heavy skillet over medium-high heat until shimmering (around 350°F–375°F).
  5. Fry: Drop heaping spoonfuls or ¼-cup scoops into the hot oil and flatten slightly with a spatula. Fry in batches without crowding for 3 to 5 minutes per side until deeply golden brown and crisp.
  6. Drain and serve: Transfer latkes to a paper towel-lined plate or wire rack, sprinkle with a pinch of salt while hot, and serve immediately with applesauce and/or sour cream with smoked salmon (or salmon roe).

B.C. Premier Lorne Doerkson has promised to mandate a return-to-office for government workers, and CHEK readers are split on their thoughts about it.

You can read more on people’s thoughts on that — as well as vertical filmmaking, the upkeep of iconic Greater Victoria signs, and federal funding for BC Ferries — below.

Rob Shaw: Incoming premier tells government workers to expect to be back in the office

Karen Schlogel writes:

The idea of requiring government workers to be back in the office full time seems a bit short-sighted to me. It puts more cars on the road, leading to increased emissions and possibly more accidents as our mornings are darker. It may also put greater stress on employees. At the very least, there should be consultation with all stakeholders.

Soccorsa Hoggard writes:

YES, lazy humans, get them back into an office, so they can be watched as they work! Let’s keep those tax dollars in the right pockets. I don’t pay anyone to sit at home in PJs, coffee in hand, telling everyone “how far it is to drive to work.” Get to work, or we will find someone more competent to fill your shoes, in an office no less!

Linda Belong writes:

I think there should be an exception for those with physical disabilities.

Antoinette DeWit writes:

I fully concur with the decision to require all employees to return to the actual place of work for which they were hired. As per usual, a few rotten eggs immediately or gradually abused the privilege of working from home. It became a nightmare for employers. Taxpayers became furious and rightly so.

Read the original story here.

Island film production company takes aim at vertical filmmaking

Helen Price writes:

Just another thing to continue shortening our attention spans. I write a blog and to keep my readers happy I have to break it up into short paragraphs and keep it short.

I have been blogging since 2006 and it’s amazing how much it has changed over the years. People can’t sit for longer than ten minutes to read an article with bigger, longer paragraphs.

I can only see why vertical filming is becoming popular. First it was YouTube videos, then shorter reels and now tiny movies…..all making our brains tinier.

Read the original story here.

Iconic Thetis Lake sign restored after more than 40 years

Miriam MacLeod writes:

This is so nice to see. Sadly, there are many signs around the highways that are aging and hard to read, due to the paint wearing off, or dirt, or overgrown bush/trees covering them up.

The other side of this story is not being told. The reason why BC Ferries is not equally funded in comparison to the ferries in Atlantic Canada is because they are ‘have not’ provinces, and are funded in part by the Canadian Equalization Program.

Provinces that have the resources to provide a higher standard of services do not receive equalization payments. British Columbia, along with Alberta and Saskatchewan, are ‘have’ provinces.

NDP MP Gord Johns is calling on the federal government to suspend planned workforce reductions at Pacific Rim National Park Reserve, warning the cuts could affect visitor safety, conservation and tourism on Vancouver Island’s west coast.

Johns, who represents Courtenay–Alberni and is the NDP’s tourism critic, says approximately 44 Pacific Rim employees – more than half of the park’s permanent workforce – have received workforce adjustment notices.

The notices do not necessarily mean layoffs, but affected employees face a Nov. 23 deadline to consider voluntary departure options without knowing which positions could ultimately be eliminated.

The cuts are part of broader Parks Canada workforce reductions across the country and include the closure of the Gulf Islands National Park Reserve’s dedicated park warden detachment.

Parks Canada has confirmed the Gulf Islands will instead be served by wardens based at Pacific Rim, which will gain one permanent position for a total of five year-round park wardens.

The decision has raised concerns about how wardens will cover the two parks, which are more than 250 kilometres apart.

Johns raised the issue in the House of Commons on Nov. 19, questioning the federal government’s decision to offer free admission to national parks through the Canada Strong Pass while reducing the staff responsible for maintaining facilities, protecting wildlife and keeping visitors safe.

“We support affordable access, I think everybody does, to our national parks, but inviting more visitors, while cutting staff puts conservation, visitor safety and rural livelihoods at risk,” Johns told the House.

Johns says Pacific Rim is a major economic driver for West Coast municipalities, supporting hotels, restaurants, tour operators and Indigenous tourism businesses. He warns that staffing reductions could affect visitor services, trail maintenance, conservation programs and emergency response, particularly as visitation to the park has increased over the past decade.

“Making our national parks free while cutting the people who protect them isn’t a conservation strategy; it’s a contradiction,” he noted in a release.

Johns also says the cuts could affect relationships with Nuu-chah-nulth First Nations, including commitments to cooperative management outlined in a 2024 memorandum of understanding with Tla-o-qui-aht First Nation.

He has written to Environment and Climate Change Minister Julie Dabrusin requesting an immediate pause on the reductions while their impacts on tourism, employment, visitor safety, conservation and Indigenous partnerships are assessed.

An Esquimalt man has been sentenced for money laundering and operating an illegal casino in Saanich more than two years after police raided the underground gambling establishment.

Bryan William Toth, 55, pleaded guilty Nov. 17 to one count of keeping a common gaming house and one count of laundering proceeds of crime, according to the Combined Forces Special Enforcement Unit of B.C. (CFSEU-BC).

Toth received a six-month conditional sentence, which he’ll serve in the community under a curfew, along with a $75,000 fine. He faces 18 months in prison if he fails to pay the fine.

The case began in January 2024, when the CFSEU-BC’s Joint Illegal Gaming Investigation Team launched a probe into a suspected underground casino operating out of a former medical clinic in the 3400-block of Cook Street.

Then in August 2024, investigators executed search warrants at the property, arresting the 14 people and also seizing two poker tables, thousands of poker chips, financial records, electronic devices and around $17,000 in cash.

Police also seized three luxury vehicles believed to be proceeds of crime: a 2024 Cadillac Lyriq, a 2020 Land Rover and a 2014 Mercedes SL550.

In November 2025, prosecutors approved three charges against Toth, including possession of proceeds of crime. He has now pleaded guilty to the other two charges.

“This outcome is a significant achievement for our investigators and reinforces that illegal gaming is not a victimless crime,” said CFSEU-BC spokesperson Sgt. Sarbjit K. Sangha in a statement Monday.

“These operations can provide opportunities for organized crime to generate and launder money.”

The investigation attracted attention in August 2024 after police described the underground gambling establishment as resembling a miniature Las Vegas casino.

But two people who told CHEK News they had attended the establishment disputed that description, saying it was primarily a place where people gathered to play poker for money.

Both acknowledged that the gambling activities were illegal.

Toth was also involved in a separate civil dispute over a Victoria property where he admitted operating unlicensed poker games between 2021 and 2023.

In August 2025, a judge dismissed both a landlord’s claims against Toth and his counterclaim, finding the landlord had overcharged him and acted deceptively. The judge also found Toth’s testimony credible, despite his admissions about the illegal gambling activities.

Police have maintained that illegal gaming operations can facilitate money laundering and other criminal activities.

“These operations can provide opportunities for organized crime to generate and launder money. This outcome demonstrates our commitment to pursuing complex investigations, following the money and holding those responsible accountable,” Sangha said.

The provincial police unit says it will continue to work with law enforcement and government to investigate and disrupt illegal gaming operations across B.C.
